headlines.title: Newsom talks climate with world leaders in New York, accuses Trump of abdicating that responsibility
headlines.description: Saying President Donald Trump has abdicated his responsibilities on climate change, California Gov. Gavin Newsom met with world and business leaders Wednesday to advance climate action and clean energy on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. State and local governments are leading, he said, as “Trump is trying to recreate the 19th century” by reopening coal plants, announcing new plans for oil drilling including off California, and centering his energy policy on fossil fuels that cause climate change. “He’s doubling down on stupid, and he’s putting the American economy at risk,” Newsom said in an interview. He called Trump the most destructive environmental president in American history and “an invasive species.” White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers used Trump’s derogatory nickname for the governor, “Newscum,” in responding to the comments. She said his “doubling down on Biden’s unpopular, unreliable and costly Green New Scam is stupid.” “No one is surprised to see him whining about the climate change hoax at another conference instead of fixing the problems plaguing his state: out-of-control crime, the highest homeless population in the United States, and wildfire victims still waiting on state permits to rebuild their homes and businesses,” Taylor wrote in an email. Newsom has long been trying to counter Trump’s climate approach Newsom, a Democrat eyeing a 2028 presidential run, has sought to counter Trump’s stance on climate issues before. He went to the U.N. climate talks hosted in Belem, Brazil in 2025 when Trump skipped it. Trump prioritizes fossil fuels to produce electricity. The Biden administration sought to ramp up clean energy as a climate change solution. Trump began reversing U.S. energy policies his first day back in office. Last year at the UN, Trump called climate change the “greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world.” He has hindered renewable energy, particularly offshore wind, while China and other countries invest heavily. China leads the world in adding wind and solar power, though it also added a lot of coal power last year. Chinese President Xi Jinping begins his state visit to Washington Wednesday. As the economic and technological competition between the countries escalates, Newsom said the Chinese leader is “cleaning our clock from an economic perspective.” Trump and Xi are expected to discuss artificial intelligence as they meet this week. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. has proposed a new “ notification mechanism ” for AI incidents that could affect national security. Newsom also not happy with Trump AI stance Newsom was critical of Trump for not doing more to add guardrails and instead listening to advice to let artificial intelligence “rip.” Newsom announced Wednesday a group of experts who will advise on oversight recommendations in California, including advancing the creation of a potential “kill switch” for rogue frontier models. Trump was in New York on Tuesday. Unlike last year’s climate-focused speech, Trump defended his actions against Iran as he spoke at the U.N. General Assembly and made the diplomatic rounds. Newsom spoke at the United Nations on Wednesday alongside mayors grappling with the impacts of climate change and calling for collective action. He shared how the state is using renewables to change the way it produces and consumes energy, while reducing carbon pollution. While in New York, he also signed a new agreement with Spain’s prime minister to strengthen collaboration on clean energy and climate issues and announced progress to link carbon markets with Washington state. “California is not going to sit back and watch this guy roll back the last half century. We’re going to lead the next great revolution,” Newsom said. “We’re going to dominate and we’re going to out compete and we are going to prepare the economy,” he said, “not just in California, but the rest of the nation, for the fierce competitive fight against China as we move forward in this space.” ___ The Associated Press’ climate and environmental coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. headlines.title: 2 men allegedly yell anti-gay slurs during on-campus beating of San Jose State student
headlines.description: Two young men face hate crime charges after they allegedly beat a San Jose State University student while yelling homophobic slurs, the Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office announced Wednesday. Sunnyvale resident Josue Medina Flores, 19, and Fremont resident Christian Gabriel Nunez Petty, 20, were charged with felony assault with hate crime allegations in connection with the unprovoked attack on the San Jose State campus early Saturday morning, the district attorney’s office said. The male student and two female friends were walking on the campus at about 3:44 a.m. when they passed by the two suspects, according to the district attorney’s office. The suspects allegedly asked the student if he was gay and yelled anti-gay slurs at him. The student and his friends ignored the suspects and continued walking. The suspects allegedly then ran up to the student and attacked him, punching him in the head more than two dozen times and kicking him while yelling anti-gay slurs, the district attorney’s office said. The suspects allegedly also struck one of the student’s friends when she jumped on top of him to shield him from the punches and kicks. The suspects fled from the scene, but San Jose State police officers managed to arrest them before they could make it off the campus, according to district attorney’s office. The student was taken to a local hospital to be treated for his injuries and later released, the district attorney’s office said. The university’s security camera network captured video footage of the attack, the district attorney’s office said. The suspects are scheduled to be arraigned Wednesday afternoon, according to the district attorney’s office. They face prison time if they are convicted. “If you hurt someone because of their race, religion, gender, or sexuality, you will be arrested and prosecuted,” District Attorney Jeff Rosen said in a statement. “Tolerance and diversity are cherished values in this community. We back up them with one voice – and the full might of the law.”

headlines.title: Woman killed after allegedly exiting vehicle following crash on Highway 101 in San Jose
headlines.description: A 63-year-old woman was killed on Highway 101 in San Jose on Monday night after allegedly exiting her vehicle following a collision. The victim was driving northbound in a Nissan Juke when she allegedly rear-ended a Toyota Prius south of Oakland Road, according to the California Highway Patrol. The driver of the Nissan got out of her vehicle and was standing in between the two disabled vehicles on the highway when another vehicle struck the Nissan, pinning the woman between her vehicle and the Prius, according to the California Highway Patrol. The woman, who the CHP said was a San Jose resident, was pronounced dead after being taken to a hospital. The CHP said drugs and alcohol did not appear to be a factor in the 11:30 p.m. wreck. The collision remained under investigation as of Tuesday.

headlines.title: Angel Island prescribed burn to resume in Marin County
headlines.description: California State Parks, Cal Fire and the Marin County Fire Department plan to resume a prescribed burn on Angel Island State Park as early as Wednesday, two weeks after the operation was paused. Angel Island is the largest island in San Francisco Bay, about one square mile, and smoke will be visible from elsewhere around the region. Residents are asked not to call 911 to report smoke from the island. A planned burn of 260 acres that began Sept. 8 was paused after discussions with the Bay Area Air District. Smoke could be visible from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on burn days and for up to three days afterward. The prescribed fire is intended to reduce grassland and coastal scrub fuel loads and lower the risk of a catastrophic wildfire on the island. The work is supported by Proposition 4, a bond approved by California voters in 2024 to fund climate resilience projects. So far, 62 acres have been completed. The agencies said renewed burning could continue through Thursday, depending on wildfire activity, staffing and equipment availability, weather, smoke movement and fuel moisture. “We really look for those small windows that have the greatest ability to disperse the smoke in the least impactful manner,” said Division Chief Graham Groneman with the Marin County Fire Department. Angel Island State Park will remain open during burn days. However, some trails near the burn area, including portions of the Ida Trail, Sunset Trail and the park’s fire and perimeter roads, will be closed for one to three days during and immediately after the burn. Access to the summit of Mount Livermore on the island will not be permitted on some burn days as well. Visitors are advised to follow posted closures and directions from park and fire personnel.

headlines.title: ‘Smart Charge Bundle' from PG&E and GM boosts EV affordability in San Ramon
headlines.description: PG&E and General Motors have announced a partnership out of San Ramon called “The Smart Charge Bundle” in an attempt to make electric cars more affordable in the Bay Area. Customers who buy or lease an electric vehicle from General Motors can receive an EV charger for free. They will also see a $15 credit on their electric bills every month. The smart technology will automatically charge vehicles when the grid has the lowest demand, saving customers even more money. Utility leaders say it’s a win-win. Customers will need to have the EV chargers installed. Anyone interested can enroll for the bundle directly through local Chevrolet, GMC or Cadillac dealerships, or log onto gmenergy.gm.com.

headlines.title: Concord barber becomes bluesman by night
headlines.description: When barber Ruben De Avila Jr. isn’t cutting hair in his Concord barbershop, there’s a good chance he’s cutting a blues riff on a stage somewhere. The second-generation barber — owner of V.I.P. Barbershop — has a second life as a blues guitarist, transforming into Jr. De Ville when he slips on his Fender Stratocaster and fronts his longtime band. To him, there’s a logical connection between the stage and the barber chair. “People choose to go to a show for their personal pleasure,” De Avila said as he snipped a customer’s hair. “And I think for barbering it’s the same thing.” De Avila has plucked almost as long as he’s cut hair. His father, Ruben De Avila Sr. has his own barbershop in Concord, and his son started cutting hair when he was fourteen years old. In high school, the football team would line-up outside the family garage on game days as De Avila Jr. trimmed and snipped the players’ hair into prime game shape. “I tried not to get into barbering after high school,” he said, “but all my friends were like, ’Why? What are you doing? You’re good at it.’” His twin passions were born about the same time. He was 16 when his musician grandfather first taught De Avila to play guitar. Then came the thunderbolt of hearing Jimi Hendrix for the first time, as well as Carlos Santana, who like De Avila, grew up in San Francisco. Ruben De Avila works as a barber during the day, and as a blues musician at night — performing under the name Jr. De Ville. “There is a big influence of his in my playing,” De Avila said, flanked by the Gibson Les Paul hanging in his shop. “Just what he put into that music and the feeling he has.” De Avila discovered the pillars of the blues — B.B. King, Junior Wells, Buddy Guy and Freddy King, which took him down his musical path of the blues. “Everybody’s gone through heartbreak and the blues is something I think every single person can relate to,” he said. “Just the soul that comes out of that music is what drove me to play it.” Like the old blues legend, De Avila eventually came to a crossroads. Should he pursue a career in music, or barbering? He graduated from cutting hair in the garage, to attending barber college, to a chair in his father’s Concord barbershop where he spent the next nine years. He cut hair in the day, and played the blues at night. After that, he went out on his own and started V.I.P. Barbershop. “I couldn’t imagine myself doing anything else,” he said, which could apply to both music and barbering. “I’ve been doing it so long.” Culture also played a big role De Avila’s upbringing. His father is Mexican-American and his mother Nicaraguan-American. His grandmother had a hair salon in San Francisco’s Mission District — where his hero Santana grew up. The heritage, and occupation that was handed-down to him has also trickled down to another generation. His son Ruben “Bubba” De Avila cuts hair in V.I.P. Barbershop and De Avila beamed as he watched his son cut hair. “It’s surreal having my son do the same thing as me and keep the family tradition going,” De Avila said. On a recent evening, Jr. De Ville was decked out in black jeans and t-shirt as he strapped on his guitar and took to the stage of the Marquee Club in Vallejo’s Empress Theater. His crack band launched into a blistering rocker as the packed room began to bob and gyrate to the smoky blues. A few tunes later, De Avila wrenched the strings and emotion from his Stratocaster in a slow blues burner, tilting back his head as his guitar whined and soared. He started the band in 1997. “Once I hit that stage I get lost,” he said. “I literally get lost in it and I leave this world for a little while.” He returns to earth the next day as he heads to his barbershop, which is decorated like a vintage blues club — inspired by a trip to the blues Mecca of Memphis. The barbershop banter is steady as he his fellow barbers and customers brush through the usual topics of football, travel and food. He laughs easily as another customer slides into his chair. “People come here, this is their getaway,” De Avila said, tying an apron to his customer. “Music is my getaway.”

headlines.title: Former San Jose high school manager pleads guilty to paying minors to make porn
headlines.description: A former operations manager at a San Jose high school pleaded guilty in federal court earlier this week to two counts of online child enticement and two counts of receipt of child pornography. The charges against 46-year-old Todd Baldwin were brought by federal prosecutors after he was accused of paying underage boys — including at least one student he knew through the school where he worked, Valley Christian High School — to take pictures and film themselves engaging in sexual acts, according to the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California’s office. Other victims attended Live Oak High School in Morgan Hill. Baldwin was accused of paying the 16- and 17-year-old victims thousands of dollars to make pornography for his consumption and to sell online. He also collected and tried to sell their used underwear, prosecutors said. He used Snapchat, Gmail, Venmo, and CashApp to communicate with the victims and transfer money to them. Baldwin faces between a decade and life in prison. He is scheduled to be sentenced in January and remains free on bond in the meantime.

headlines.title: Local coalition calls for end to federal oversight of Oakland police
headlines.description: More than two decades after the “Oakland Riders” scandal rocked the Oakland Police Department, the city could be moving closer to running its police department without federal oversight, with a judge expected to make that decision next week. The scandal included allegations of false arrests, planted evidence and excessive force. Four officers were prosecuted for felony misconduct. There were no convictions, but a class action lawsuit on behalf of 119 people ended with the city paying an $11 million settlement. Over the past 23 years, the Oakland Police Department has undergone 51 court-ordered reforms. Next week’s hearing is set for Tuesday, and the judge is expected to approve OPD’s release from federal oversight. On Wednesday, members of Safe Oakland, a coalition of neighborhood, business, civil rights and faith leaders, addressed the reforms enacted over the past two decades and shared why they believe the police department should be trusted to operate without federal oversight – with a few qualifiers. “We are the communities that paid the price, and this morning we are here to say it is time and to say exactly what Oakland must do to make sure we never go back,” Evergreen Missionary Baptist Church Sr. Bishop L. Lawrence Brandon said. Safe Oakland does want the city to continue public reporting of internal affairs cases, use of force incidents and racial disparities in traffic stops. “We want a police department that is effective in protecting our neighborhoods, and we want a police department that respects the rights of every person and is held accountable when those standards are not met,” Yemeni community leader and small business owner Ali Albasier said. The group also called for continued transparency to make sure OPD abides by the California Public Records Act and civilian oversight by the police commission and the Office of Inspector General. “Oakland voters created these positions so that when the monitor leaves, we have the ability to monitor,” Black Action Alliance interim CEO Loren Taylor said. The group also wants the city to track key accountability indicators and let the public know if the department is trending in the wrong direction. Members said a main part of community oversight restructuring should include standing conversations with local civil rights branches and faith groups. “A safer city begins with a community that cares,” Brandon said. NBC Bay Area reached out to OPD for comment on the Safe Oakland oversight concerns but did not immediately hear back. Oakland May 27 Oakland Jun 1, 2022

headlines.title: Divers search South Bay Lake for missing San Jose man Larry Nguyen
headlines.description: The search for a missing man brought Santa Clara County Sheriff’s divers to a South Bay lake Tuesday. Crews from the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office were seen searching Grant Lake on Mount Hamilton Road, looking for any signs of Larry Nguyen. A missing person poster has been put up near the site, noting that Nguyen was last seen on Sept. 8 when he was dropped off in a nearby parking lot. In a statement, the San Jose Police Department would only say this is an active and ongoing missing persons investigation. There is no word on whether divers found anything in the lake.

headlines.title: Ripley's Believe It or Not! to close Fisherman's Wharf location after nearly 60 years
headlines.description: After nearly six decades in operation, Ripley’s Believe It or Not! is shutting down its iconic Fisherman’s Wharf location. Jim Pattison Jr., president of Ripley’s Believe It or Not! World Entertainment, announced in a statement released Tuesday that the attraction will permanently close sometime before the end of the year.

headlines.title: Mexican Navy's ‘Cuauhtémoc' ship sails under Golden Gate Bridge ahead of 4-day visit
headlines.description: A Mexican Navy tall ship sailed into San Francisco Bay on Wednesday morning for a four-day goodwill visit, marking its first return to the city in 17 years. The ARM Cuauhtémoc BE-01 sailed beneath the Golden Gate Bridge around 8:45 a.m. before arriving at Pier 15 along The Embarcadero. The three-masted Navy training ship was greeted with fanfare as it made its official return to San Francisco. Officials from the Mexican Consulate and representatives from city government were on hand to welcome the ship, along with hundreds of crew members aboard. The visit comes after a tragic chapter in the ship’s recent history. Last year, the Cuauhtémoc struck New York’s Brooklyn Bridge, killing two people on board. The ship was commissioned in the 1980s and built in Spain. It travels to ports around the world on goodwill visits aimed at sharing Mexican culture and history. Visitors in San Francisco will have several opportunities to tour the ship during its stay. Tours are scheduled for noon to 3:30 p.m. Wednesday; 10 a.m. to noon and 4 to 8 p.m. Thursday; and 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday. The Cuauhtémoc is scheduled to depart San Francisco at 9:30 a.m. Sunday. Bay City News contributed to this report

headlines.title: Stanford University removes promotional photo altered with AI to replace student, violating policy
headlines.description: Stanford University removed a promotional photo that had been digitally altered to replace a male Hispanic student with an AI-generated Black female student without disclosure, violating university policy. The altered image breached Stanford’s policy prohibiting the use of artificial intelligence in photographs depicting people or events. Following the incident, the university removed the image and announced plans to provide additional staff training to prevent future violations.
